metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% for high-sentiment periods.
- After a price spike (e.g., >45), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect — apply a “cool-down” adjustment: reduce forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7), model forecasts are too optimistic; apply a downward bias of 1–3% to the first 5–7 days of the forecast horizon.
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., < -0.3) and price is trending down, model often fails to reflect mean reversion — increase forecast by 1–2% for the first 3–5 days to account for potential rebound.
- Model underestimates late-period prices (last 5–7 days of 30d) — especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — add 1–2% to the final 5–7 days of forecast to capture tail behavior.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days to reflect sentiment momentum.
